standard_prerequisites.name: Filtration as in property (P)
standard_prerequisites.statement: An exhaustive increasing filtration of P by dg submodules whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifted copies of A.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the successive inclusions F_i P -> F_{i+1} P that the construction of the two maps uses (source lines 2426-2432, 2440-2446).

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible short exact sequence of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: A short exact sequence of dg modules which splits as graded modules, so that the middle term is the direct sum of the outer terms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The conclusion is precisely that this sequence is admissible, which is proved by writing down the splitting (source lines 2434-2436, 2446-2448).

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of the successive inclusions
standard_prerequisites.statement: For each i the inclusion F_i P -> F_{i+1} P admits a graded left inverse s_i.
standard_prerequisites.use: The composed maps s_{j,i} and the tuple formula for the left inverse are built from those s_i (source lines 2444-2448).

core_obligations: Define the two maps: let the second map be the direct sum of the inclusion maps F_i P -> P, and let the first map act on the i-th summand of the source as the identity minus the inclusion F_i P -> F_{i+1} P (source lines 2440-2443).

Check exactness: note that the composite of the first map with the second is zero summand by summand, so that the direct sum of the steps maps onto P with kernel containing the image of the first map (source lines 2442-2444).

Exhibit the splitting: choose graded left inverses s_i of the successive inclusions, compose them into maps s_{j,i}, and verify that the formula sending x in F_j P to the tuple of its images under s_{j,0}, ..., s_{j,j-1} followed by zeros is a left inverse of the first map (source lines 2444-2448).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the surjection as the sum of inclusions and the first map by the identity minus the next inclusion on each summand.
Check that the composite is zero, so the sequence is exact.
Use the s_i and their compositions to write an explicit left inverse of the first map.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-property-P-sequence at source lines 2424-2436: for a dg A-module P with a filtration as in property (P), the direct sum of the filtration steps maps onto P and the kernel of that map is again the direct sum of the steps, so that one obtains an admissible short exact sequence of dg A-modules. The proof at source lines 2438-2448 is a construction: it defines the surjection as the direct sum of the inclusion maps, and then defines the map out of the direct sum into itself whose component on the i-th summand is the identity minus the inclusion of the i-th step into the next step, which makes the composite zero exactly on the nose. To see that the sequence splits as graded modules it chooses left inverses s_i of the successive inclusions, composes them into maps from a later step to an earlier one, and exhibits an explicit left inverse of the first arrow by sending a homogeneous element in the j-th step to the tuple of its images under the composed splittings. The whole content is in that explicit formula for the splitting, which the statement does not display. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
